q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Part A of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of Coaching earnings.
2. Part B of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of Sundry other earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: Part A of the Traffic Book deals with apportionment of Coaching earnings. Statement 2 is false: Part B deals with Goods earnings, not Sundry other earnings.

q: Refunds of fares and freight granted by the Railways are accounted for as:

options.B: A deduction from (minus entry under) the earnings of the Railways
options.D: A suspense item pending recovery

e: Refunds of fares and freight are not working expenditure; they are accounted for as a deduction (minus entry) from the earnings to which they relate.

q: Receipts from parcels and luggage traffic are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.D: Miscellaneous capital receipts

e: Parcels and luggage are coaching services, so their receipts are classified under Other Coaching Earnings, not Goods or Sundry earnings.

q: In the context of the Railway Codes, 'ACS' stands for:

options.D: Advance Correction Slip

e: In the Railway Codes, ACS stands for Advance Correction Slip, the medium through which amendments and corrections to the codes are notified.

q: Under the door-step banking arrangement, station earnings collected by the accredited bank are deposited in the Railways' current account styled:

options.D: Rail Nidhi Account

e: Under door-step banking, station earnings collected by the accredited bank are deposited in the Railways' current account styled the Rail Shakti Account.

q: The inclusion of a work in the Pink Book (Works Programme):

options.A: Amounts to sanction of the work by the Railway Board
options.B: Does not by itself amount to sanction; the work requires sanction of the competent authority before expenditure is incurred
options.C: Dispenses with the preparation of estimates for the work
options.D: Authorises the executive to re-appropriate funds to the work

e: Inclusion in the Pink Book is only inclusion in the Works Programme; it does not by itself amount to sanction, and the work still requires sanction of the competent authority before expenditure is incurred.

q: In the Works Programme, the 'throw-forward' represents:

options.A: The new works proposed for the year
options.B: The savings expected from works in progress
options.C: The balance cost of works already in progress which will spill over into the next financial year
options.D: The works completed during the year

e: The throw-forward is the balance cost of works already in progress which will spill over (remain to be spent) in the next financial year, as distinct from new works proposed.

q: An 'umbrella work' in the Pink Book is:

options.A: A single work costing more than the prescribed limit, shown individually
options.B: A deposit work executed for an outside party
options.D: A group of similar small works provided for together with a lumpsum provision under one head

e: An umbrella work groups a number of similar small works together under one head with a lumpsum provision, instead of listing each small work individually in the Pink Book.

q: Re-appropriation orders in respect of a grant for a financial year can be issued:

options.A: At any time during the following year
options.B: Only up to the close of that financial year; after 31 March the unspent grant lapses
options.C: Within three months after the close of the year
options.D: Only with the approval of Parliament

e: Re-appropriation is valid only within the financial year; after 31 March the unspent grant lapses, so re-appropriation orders cannot be issued for a closed year.

q: The system of proportionate (period-wise) allotment of funds during the year is intended mainly to:

options.B: Fix the proportions of the Primary Units
options.C: Regulate the pace of expenditure during the year so that grants are not exhausted prematurely and the ways-and-means position is watched
options.D: Distribute the plan outlay among the Plan Heads

e: Proportionate (period-wise) allotment spreads the grant over the year so that expenditure is paced evenly, grants are not exhausted prematurely, and the ways-and-means position is watched continuously.

q: An 'economy cut' motion moved during the voting of Demands for Grants proposes that the amount of the Demand be reduced:

options.D: By a specified amount, in order to effect economy in expenditure

e: An economy cut proposes reduction of the Demand by a specified amount, its object being to effect economy in the expenditure covered by the Demand.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'Appropriation' from a 'Grant'?

options.A: A grant is authorised by the Appropriation Act, while an appropriation is voted by the Lok Sabha
options.B: A grant is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand, while the appropriation is the amount authorised by the Appropriation Act, covering both the voted grants and the charged expenditure
options.C: There is no difference; the two terms are interchangeable
options.D: An appropriation relates only to revenue expenditure, while a grant relates only to capital expenditure

e: A Grant is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand; the Appropriation is the amount authorised by the Appropriation Act, which covers both the voted grants and the charged expenditure.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume I, mainly contains:

options.A: The rules and regulations governing the financial management of the Railways, including the delegation of financial powers
options.B: The lists of Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units of classification
options.C: The rules governing the purchase and custody of stores
options.D: The rules relating to Traffic Accounts and the Traffic Book

e: The Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume I, contains the rules and regulations governing the financial management of the Railways, including the delegation of financial powers.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Volume I of the Indian Railway Accounts Code contains the rules relating to the general accounts of the Railways, including the maintenance of books and the rendering of the Account Current.
2. Volume II of the Indian Railway Accounts Code deals with Traffic Accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: Volume I of the Indian Railway Accounts Code covers the general accounts, books and the Account Current, while Volume II deals with Traffic Accounts.

q: The proposals and estimates contained in the Railway Budget are explained, for the information of Parliament, in the document known as the:

options.D: Book of Demands

e: The Explanatory Memorandum explains the proposals and estimates contained in the Budget for the information of Parliament.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the Contingency Fund of India is classified under Major Head:
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, the Contingency Fund of India is classified under Major Head 8000.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, 'Civil Deposits' are classified under Major Head:
e: Civil Deposits, such as deposits of contractors and other parties, are classified under Major Head 8443 in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: 'Cash Remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same accounting authority' are classified in the Government List of Major and Minor Heads under Major Head:
e: Cash remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same accounting authority are classified under Major Head 8782.

q: The debit balance under 'Stores Suspense' (Plan Head 71) in the railway accounts represents:

options.A: Stores purchased but not yet paid for
options.B: The value of stores held in stock in the stores depots
options.C: Stores issued to works but not yet finally adjusted
options.D: Amounts recoverable from suppliers of stores

e: The debit balance under Stores Suspense represents the value of stores physically held in stock in the stores depots, awaiting issue to works or services.

q: The balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense' in the railway accounts represents:

options.A: The cost of jobs still in progress (work-in-progress) in the workshops
options.B: The value of finished products awaiting sale to outside parties
options.C: Amounts due from other railways for workshop jobs done for them
options.D: The depreciation accumulated on workshop plant and machinery

e: The balance under Manufacturing Suspense represents the cost of jobs still in progress (work-in-progress) in the workshops, which will be adjusted on completion of the jobs.

q: In the books of the Railway Board, inter-railway transfer transactions are finally adjusted under the head:

options.D: Transfer Railways

e: In the Railway Board's books, inter-railway transfer transactions are finally adjusted under the head Transfer Railways.

q: In the classification of railway accounts, the Sub-Heads and Detailed Heads below the Minor Head serve to:

options.A: Indicate the fund from which the expenditure is met
options.B: Identify the specific activity, work or unit to which the expenditure relates
options.C: Distinguish voted expenditure from charged expenditure
options.D: Indicate the object of the expenditure

e: Below the Minor Head, Sub-Heads and Detailed Heads identify the specific activity, work or unit to which the expenditure relates, giving finer detail within the functional classification.

q: An 'Interim Budget', presented in an election year, differs from a 'Vote on Account' mainly in that the Interim Budget:

options.A: Is presented only for the Railways
options.B: Does not require any vote of Parliament at all
options.C: Presents the estimates of receipts and expenditure for the whole financial year, though major policy changes are generally avoided
options.D: Covers expenditure for a period of two months only

e: An Interim Budget presents estimates of receipts and expenditure for the whole financial year (major policy changes generally being avoided in an election year), whereas a Vote on Account covers only a part of the year.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the budget proposals of the Railways are presented to Parliament:

options.A: By the Finance Minister, as part of the Union Budget
options.B: By the Railway Minister, on a separate day fixed for the Railways
options.D: By the Minister of State for Finance alone

e: After the merger, the Railways' budget proposals are presented by the Finance Minister as part of the Union Budget, the separate Railway Budget having been discontinued from 2017-18.

q: As a general rule of Government accounting, expenditure in anticipation of a grant:

options.A: Is freely permissible at the discretion of the head of the office
options.B: Is permissible up to 5 per cent of the grant
options.C: Is permissible in the month of March only
options.D: Is not permissible — expenditure can be incurred only after the grant has been authorised, the advance from the Contingency Fund of India being the recognised exception

e: Expenditure can be incurred only after the grant has been authorised; incurring expenditure in anticipation of a grant is not permissible, the recognised exception being an advance from the Contingency Fund of India.

q: An outstanding item under a suspense head which is ultimately found to be irrecoverable may be written off:

options.A: By the dealing assistant in the Accounts Office
options.B: Only under the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Automatically at the close of the financial year
options.D: Only with the approval of Parliament

e: An irrecoverable suspense item cannot be written off at lower levels; it requires the sanction of the competent authority, since the write-off extinguishes a Government claim.

q: In the case of a 'deposit work' executed by the Railways for an outside party, the amount deposited by the party is credited to the 'Deposits' head and:

options.A: The expenditure incurred on the work is debited to the same head, so that the work does not become a charge on railway revenues
options.B: The expenditure on the work is charged to the ordinary working expenses of the Railways
options.C: The deposit is treated as part of the earnings of the Railways
options.D: The expenditure on the work is charged to Capital

e: For a deposit work, the party's deposit is credited to Deposits and the expenditure on the work is debited to the same head, so the work is executed at the party's cost and does not become a charge on railway revenues.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The accounts of the Government, including the Railways, are maintained broadly on the cash basis.
2. Under the cash basis, a receipt is brought to account when the money is actually received and a payment when it is actually made, and not when the corresponding liability accrues.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: Government accounts, including the Railways, are maintained broadly on the cash basis - a receipt is accounted when money is actually received and a payment when actually made, not when the liability accrues.

q: The distinction between 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan' expenditure in the Government Budget was discontinued with effect from the financial year:
e: The Plan and Non-Plan distinction in the Government Budget was discontinued from the financial year 2017-18, the same year as the Railway Budget merger and the advancement of the Budget date.

q: A 'Vote on Account' is normally taken to authorise expenditure for a period of about:

options.D: The whole financial year

e: A Vote on Account is normally taken in an election year (or pending the full Budget) to authorise expenditure for about two months of the new financial year.

q: Supplementary grants voted by Parliament during the year are given legal effect through:

options.A: An Appropriation Act passed for the purpose
options.B: A resolution of the Railway Board
options.C: The Finance Accounts of the year
options.D: A correction slip to the Finance Code

e: Supplementary grants voted by Parliament are given legal effect through an Appropriation Act, which authorises the withdrawal of the additional amounts from the Consolidated Fund.

q: The mere existence of provision in the sanctioned Budget for an item of expenditure:

options.A: Amounts to sanction for incurring the expenditure
options.B: Dispenses with the need for preparing an estimate for the work
options.C: Authorises the executive to invite tenders for the work
options.D: Does not by itself amount to sanction — the sanction of the competent authority is separately necessary before the expenditure is incurred

e: Budget provision is only an allocation of funds; it does not by itself amount to sanction, and the sanction of the competent authority is separately necessary before expenditure is incurred.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Debt heads record transactions representing definite liabilities of the Government, or amounts recoverable by it, such as deposits and provident fund balances.
2. Suspense heads record transactions only temporarily, pending their adjustment to the final heads of account concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: Debt heads record definite liabilities of, or amounts recoverable by, Government (deposits, provident funds), while Suspense heads hold transactions only temporarily pending adjustment to their final heads.

q: Remittance heads of account are operated in the books primarily to:

options.A: Record the earnings collected at stations
options.B: Record transactions in the course of settlement between accounting units — moneys remitted from one accounting circle to another, pending final adjustment
options.C: Record the loans raised by the Railways from the market
options.D: Record expenditure on the construction of new lines

e: Remittance heads record transactions in the course of settlement between accounting units - moneys remitted from one accounting circle to another - pending their final adjustment.

q: Before the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways are voted by the Lok Sabha, they are examined in detail by:

options.A: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways
options.C: The Estimates Committees of the State Legislatures
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Before voting, the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways are examined in detail by the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways, which reports to Parliament.

q: In voting on a Demand for Grant, the Lok Sabha may assent to the Demand, refuse it or reduce the amount demanded, but it cannot:

options.B: Move a cut motion on the Demand
options.C: Reduce the Demand to Re 1 by a policy cut
options.D: Increase the amount of the Demand

e: The Lok Sabha may assent to a Demand, refuse it or reduce it, but it cannot increase the amount demanded, since the Demand represents the executive's proposal made on the President's recommendation.

q: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, the Finance Bill, which gives effect to the taxation proposals of the Budget, must be passed by Parliament within:

options.D: 120 days of its introduction

e: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, a declared provision of the Finance Bill has immediate provisional effect, but the Bill must be passed within 75 days of its introduction, failing which the provision ceases to have effect.

q: Article 114(2) of the Constitution bars any amendment to the Appropriation Bill which would have the effect of:

options.A: Laying the Bill before the President for assent
options.B: Varying the amount, or altering the destination, of any grant already made by the House
options.C: Discussing the Bill in the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Printing the Bill in the Gazette

e: Article 114(2) bars any amendment to the Appropriation Bill that would vary the amount, or alter the destination, of any grant already made by the House.

q: In the Budget documents (Demands for Grants), expenditure 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India is distinguished from voted expenditure by being:

options.C: Shown in a separate volume altogether
options.D: Omitted from the Demands for Grants

e: In the Demands for Grants, expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund is printed in italics to distinguish it from the voted expenditure, which the Lok Sabha alone votes.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Appropriation Accounts of a zonal railway are prepared by the Accounts Department of the railway.
2. The Appropriation Accounts are audited on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India before they are presented to Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: the Appropriation Accounts of a zonal railway are prepared by its Accounts Department, and they are audited on behalf of the CAG before being presented to Parliament.

q: 'Cash-in-Transit' in the railway accounts is classified under the:

options.D: Remittance heads

e: Cash-in-Transit, being money in the course of movement between accounting units or to the bank, is classified under the Remittance heads of account.

q: The receipts and payments of the Railways are conducted:

options.A: Through Government treasuries, like those of other Government departments
options.B: Through the banking system — the Reserve Bank of India and the accredited bank
options.C: In cash only, through the Cash & Pay Office
options.D: Through the State Bank of India alone, the Railways having no account with the Reserve Bank

e: Railway receipts and payments are conducted through the banking system - the Reserve Bank of India and the accredited bank - and not through Government treasuries as in other departments.

q: The Final Works Programme of a zonal railway for a year is finalised:

options.A: After the approval of the Budget and the communication of the budget allotment for the year
options.B: Before the Budget Estimates for the year are framed
options.C: Only after the close of the financial year
options.D: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts

e: The Final Works Programme of a zonal railway is finalised only after the Budget is approved and the year's budget allotment is communicated, so that works are matched to the funds actually available.

q: The lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation comprise a capital (principal) component and an interest (finance charge) component. The interest component is charged to:

options.C: Revenue — the working expenses of the Railways
options.D: The Development Fund

e: IRFC lease charges have two components: the capital component is charged under Plan Head 22, while the interest (finance charge) component is charged to Revenue as working expenses.

q: Which of the following receipts is classified under 'Sundry Other Earnings' of the Railways?

options.D: Rent received for railway land and buildings let out to outsiders

e: Rent received for railway land and buildings let out to outsiders is not traffic earnings; it is classified under Sundry Other Earnings.

q: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was enhanced in the year 2021 to:

options.D: Rs 1,00,000 crore

e: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was enhanced in 2021 from Rs 500 crore to Rs 30,000 crore to give the Government greater room for unforeseen expenditure.

q:
Consider the following principles of Government budgeting:
1. Annuality — the authorisation of Parliament to incur expenditure is valid for one financial year only.
2. Gross budgeting — the estimates of expenditure are framed in gross terms, without netting off the related receipts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true budgeting principles: annuality means Parliament's authorisation is valid for one financial year only, and gross budgeting means estimates are framed gross, without netting off related receipts.

q: Within each Demand for Grant presented to Parliament, the estimates of 'charged' expenditure and 'voted' expenditure are:

options.B: Always merged into a single figure
options.C: Shown only in the Finance Bill
options.D: Shown only in the case of the Railways

e: Within each Demand for Grant, charged expenditure (not subject to vote) and voted expenditure are shown separately, as the Constitution treats them differently.

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the minor head bearing the code '800' is generally used for:

options.D: 'Other receipts' or 'Other expenditure' not covered by any specific minor head

e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, minor head 800 is the residual head used for "Other receipts" or "Other expenditure" not covered by any specific minor head.

q: The Economic Survey, reviewing the state of the economy, is presented to Parliament:

options.B: Shortly before the presentation of the Union Budget
options.C: At the end of the financial year
options.D: Only once in five years

e: The Economic Survey, which reviews the state of the economy, is presented to Parliament shortly before the presentation of the Union Budget.

q: The Appropriation Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha after the Demands for Grants have been voted is categorised as:

options.D: A Private Member's Bill

e: The Appropriation Bill is a Money Bill, since it deals with withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, and is introduced only in the Lok Sabha.

q: A 'policy cut' motion on a Demand for Grant is moved in order to:

options.C: Express disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand
options.D: Effect economy in expenditure

e: A policy cut is moved to express disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand, and accordingly proposes reducing the Demand to Re 1.

q: A 'token cut' motion on a Demand for Grant is moved primarily in order to:

options.A: Express disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand
options.D: Ventilate a specific grievance against the Government

e: A token cut, proposing a reduction of Rs 100, is moved primarily to ventilate a specific grievance against the Government within the scope of the Demand.

q: The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are laid before Parliament together with:

options.A: The Pink Book for the year
options.B: The Audit Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on those accounts
options.C: The Outcome Budget for the year
options.D: The report of the Railway Convention Committee

e: The Appropriation Accounts are laid before Parliament together with the Audit Report of the CAG on those accounts, so that variations between grants and actuals are examined with audit comments.

q: The annual appropriation from revenue to the Railway Pension Fund is assessed with reference to:

options.A: The gross earnings of the year
options.B: The dividend liability of the Railways
options.C: The actuarial valuation of the pension liability
options.D: The balance available in the Development Fund

e: The annual appropriation to the Railway Pension Fund is assessed on the basis of the actuarial valuation of the pension liability, unlike the DRF, which is based on the cost and codal life of assets.

q: In the allocation of a capital work, such as 'DRF-3100' or 'Capital-1100', the element appearing before the Plan Head indicates:

options.A: The source of finance (fund) from which the work is financed
options.B: The zonal railway executing the work
options.C: The year in which the work was sanctioned
options.D: The Primary Unit of the work

e: In an allocation like DRF-3100 or Capital-1100, the element before the Plan Head (DRF, Capital, etc.) indicates the source of finance - the fund from which the work is financed.

q: The complete allocation of an item of revenue expenditure indicates, in order:

options.A: Major Head - Sub-Major Head - Minor Head - Primary Unit
options.B: Primary Unit - Minor Head - Sub-Major Head - Major Head
options.C: Plan Head - Sub-Major Head - Primary Unit - Minor Head
options.D: Major Head - Plan Head - Minor Head - Primary Unit

e: The complete allocation of revenue expenditure runs in the order: Major Head, Sub-Major Head, Minor Head and Primary Unit - from the broad function down to the object of expenditure.

q: Works relating to railway research are classified under Plan Head:
e: Works relating to railway research (such as RDSO research schemes) are classified under Plan Head 18.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the State Provident Funds, including the State Railway Provident Fund, are classified under Major Head:
e: The State Provident Funds, including the State Railway Provident Fund, are classified under Major Head 8009 in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The list of Primary Units is uniform for all zonal railways and applies across the Sub-Major Heads.
2. A zonal railway may create new Primary Units to suit its local requirements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the list of Primary Units is uniform for all zonal railways and applies across the Sub-Major Heads. Statement 2 is false: a zonal railway cannot create new Primary Units on its own.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Revenue expenditure is classified under Major Head 5002 by Plan Heads
options.B: Both revenue and capital expenditure are classified under Major Head 3002
options.C: Plan Heads are used only for revenue expenditure
options.D: Capital (works) expenditure is classified under Major Head 5002 by Plan Heads, while revenue expenditure is classified under Major Head 3002 by Sub-Major Heads

e: Inspection and acceptance of the work by the Railway do not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the quality and soundness of the work; liability for defects remains with him.

q: Repairs and maintenance of residential buildings (staff quarters) are classified under Major Head 3002 as part of Sub-Major Head:
e: Repairs and maintenance of residential buildings (staff quarters) fall under Sub-Major Head 02 of Major Head 3002, which covers repairs and maintenance of buildings and structures.

q: Expenditure on railway hospitals and health services for staff is classified under Major Head 3002 under Sub-Major Head:
e: Expenditure on railway hospitals and staff health services is classified under Sub-Major Head 09 of Major Head 3002, covering staff welfare and amenities including medical services.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For revenue expenditure, the unit of appropriation is the Sub-Major Head.
2. For capital/works expenditure, the unit of appropriation is the Primary Unit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: for revenue expenditure, the Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation. Statement 2 is false: for capital/works expenditure the unit of appropriation is the Plan Head, not the Primary Unit.

q: Major Heads 8658 (Suspense Accounts), 8675 (Deposits with Reserve Bank) and 8782 (Cash Remittances) in the Government List of Major and Minor Heads all fall under the section of the Public Account relating to:

options.D: Suspense and Miscellaneous

e: Major Heads 8658, 8675 and 8782 are all placed in the "Suspense and Miscellaneous" section of the Public Account in the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is charged to the working expenses of the Railways, whether or not there is a surplus.
2. Appropriations to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund are made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: appropriation to the DRF is a charge on working expenses and is made whether or not there is a surplus, whereas the Development Fund and Capital Fund are appropriated out of the surplus (net revenue).

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Debt Service Fund is credited with the proceeds of market borrowings raised through IRFC.
2. The Debt Service Fund is intended to provide a cushion for meeting the Railways' debt-service obligations in years when revenues are inadequate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: the Debt Service Fund is built up by appropriations, not credited directly with IRFC borrowing proceeds. Statement 2 is true: it provides a cushion for meeting debt-service obligations in years when revenues are inadequate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The commuted value of pension paid to a retiring railway servant is debited to the Railway Pension Fund.
2. Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity is charged directly to the working expenses under Sub-Major Head 11.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the commuted value of pension is debited to the Railway Pension Fund. Statement 2 is false: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity is also borne by the Pension Fund, not charged directly to working expenses.

q: The accumulations of a railway servant under the National Pension System are:

options.A: Held in the Railway Pension Fund
options.B: Held in the State Railway Provident Fund
options.C: Transferred to the NPS Trust and invested through the pension fund managers
options.D: Retained permanently in the Public Account of India

e: NPS accumulations of a railway servant are transferred to the NPS Trust and invested through the pension fund managers; they are not held in the Pension Fund or the Provident Fund.

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund, set up in 2001-02, was created on the recommendations of:

options.B: The Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee)
options.D: The Rakesh Mohan Committee

e: The SRSF was created on the recommendations of the Railway Safety Review Committee, chaired by Justice Khanna, which had examined railway safety and the backlog of asset renewals.

q: An 'Exceptional Grant' voted by the Lok Sabha under Article 116 of the Constitution is a grant made:

options.A: For a purpose which forms no part of the current service of any financial year
options.B: For a part of the financial year, pending the passing of the Budget
options.C: To meet an unexpected demand upon the resources of India
options.D: To regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of a grant

e: An Exceptional Grant under Article 116 is made for a purpose which forms no part of the current service of any financial year - a purpose outside the normal services of the year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Excess expenditure over a grant is regularised by the Railway Board through re-appropriation in the following year.
2. The Demand for an Excess Grant is presented to the Lok Sabha after the excess has been examined by the Public Accounts Committee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: excess expenditure cannot be regularised by the Railway Board through re-appropriation. Statement 2 is true: the Demand for an Excess Grant is presented to the Lok Sabha after the Public Accounts Committee has examined the excess.

q: The Appropriation Act, besides authorising withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, contains:

options.A: The taxation proposals of the Government
options.B: A Schedule specifying the services/purposes and the amounts appropriated for each
options.C: The list of works included in the Pink Book
options.D: The report of the Comptroller and Auditor General

e: Besides authorising withdrawals, the Appropriation Act contains a Schedule specifying the services and purposes and the amounts appropriated for each, as voted or charged.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha can discuss the Budget but has no power to vote on the Demands for Grants.
2. Cut motions on Demands for Grants can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: the Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on Demands for Grants, and cut motions, which arise on Demands, can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.

q: The single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways is divided into two sections, namely:

options.D: Revenue and Capital

e: The single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways is divided into two sections - Revenue and Capital - reflecting the two broad categories of railway expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross Budgetary Support provided to the Railways forms part of their Capital-at-charge.
2. Extra Budgetary Resources raised through IRFC also form part of the Capital-at-charge of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: Gross Budgetary Support is Government investment and forms part of Capital-at-charge. Statement 2 is false: Extra Budgetary Resources raised through IRFC are borrowings/leases and do not form part of Capital-at-charge.

q: The detailed break-up of the estimates included in the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways is published in the document called:

options.D: Budget at a Glance

e: The detailed break-up of the estimates in the Railway Demands is published in the Detailed Demands for Grants, which give the head-wise and activity-wise details behind the summary figures.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Main Cash Book and the Journal Book are Subsidiary Books of a railway.
2. The Ledger is a General Book and not a Subsidiary Book.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: the Main Cash Book and the Journal Book are Subsidiary Books of a railway, while the Ledger, which collects the classified accounts, is a General Book.

q: Amounts due by the Railways to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment, are credited to the head:

options.D: Demands Payable

e: Amounts due by the Railways to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment, are credited to Demands Payable, the counterpart of Demands Recoverable.

q: The Debt Head Report showing the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads is rendered:

options.B: Monthly, along with the Account Current
options.D: Only at the close of the financial year

e: The Debt Head Report, showing balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, is rendered monthly along with the Account Current so that outstanding balances are reviewed every month.

q: The balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in the books of a zonal railway is reconciled periodically with:

options.A: The figures intimated by the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: The Cash Book of the Cash & Pay Office
options.C: The Asset Registers maintained by the executive departments
options.D: The Pink Book maintained in the Railway Board

e: The balance under Deposits with Reserve Bank is reconciled periodically with the figures intimated by the Reserve Bank of India, ensuring the railway's books agree with the bank's record.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The initial records of transactions, such as bills, vouchers and measurement books, are prepared by the executive departments.
2. The Accounts Department itself prepares all the initial records of transactions of a railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: initial records such as bills, vouchers and measurement books originate in the executive departments. Statement 2 is false: the Accounts Department compiles accounts from these records; it does not prepare all of them itself.

q: The 'net revenue' of the Railways for a year is arrived at by deducting from the gross earnings:

options.A: The dividend payable to General Finances only
options.B: The capital expenditure of the year
options.C: The amount of Gross Budgetary Support received
options.D: The total working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund

e: Net revenue is gross earnings minus total working expenses, which include the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund; dividend is then payable out of this net revenue.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Operating Ratio expresses the working expenses of the Railways as a percentage of their gross earnings.
2. A lower Operating Ratio indicates a better financial performance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: the Operating Ratio expresses working expenses as a percentage of gross earnings, and a lower ratio means expenses absorb a smaller share of earnings, indicating better financial performance.

q: The earnings of the Railways are brought to account:

options.A: Only when the cash is actually received at stations
options.B: On the basis of the traffic booked (accrual basis), irrespective of when the cash is collected
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year
options.D: On the basis of the Budget Estimates

e: Railway earnings are brought to account on the accrual basis - on the traffic booked - irrespective of when the cash is actually collected at stations or from parties.

q: A cut motion cannot be moved in respect of:

options.A: A Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Railways
options.B: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: A Demand relating to working expenses

e: Charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha, so no cut motion can be moved on it; cut motions can be moved only on voted Demands.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A supplementary grant is required when the amount authorised for a service is found to be insufficient during the year.
2. A supplementary grant is also required for expenditure on a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: a supplementary grant is needed when the authorised amount proves insufficient during the year, and also for expenditure on a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) is financed through:

options.A: A surcharge on passenger fares only
options.B: Gross Budgetary Support and the Railways' internal resources
options.D: Fines and penalties collected by the Railways

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is financed through Gross Budgetary Support from the Government and the Railways' own internal resources.

q: The unspent balances of the Railway Funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Development Fund, at the close of a financial year:

options.A: Lapse like the balances of grants
options.B: Are transferred to the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Are divided among the zonal railways
options.D: Do not lapse and are carried forward in the Public Account

e: Unlike grant balances, the unspent balances of the Railway Funds do not lapse at the close of the year; they are carried forward in the Public Account for use in later years.

q: The expenditure of the Railway Board and other central organisations of the Railways, such as RDSO, is classified under Major Head:
e: Expenditure of the Railway Board and central organisations like RDSO is classified under Major Head 3001, which covers the policy formulation, direction and miscellaneous organisation of Indian Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The accounts of the Railways are maintained on commercial principles, with a Balance Sheet of assets and liabilities.
2. The railway accounts nevertheless form part of the Government accounts of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: the Railways maintain their accounts on commercial principles, including a Balance Sheet of assets and liabilities, yet the railway accounts form part of the Government accounts of India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Remittances into Banks' is a suspense head of account.
2. 'Reserve Bank Suspense' is a suspense head of account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: Remittances into Banks is a remittance head, not a suspense head. Statement 2 is true: Reserve Bank Suspense is a suspense head, holding transactions pending clearance by the RBI.

q: For works included in the Works Programme (Pink Book) which have not yet been sanctioned, the budget makes only:

options.D: A provision under a suspense head

e: For works included in the Works Programme which have not yet been sanctioned, only a token provision is made in the Budget, the full provision following after sanction.

q: Interest during construction, that is, interest on capital borrowed for a work during its construction period, is:

options.A: Charged to the working expenses of the year
options.C: Treated as part of the cost of the work and charged to Capital
options.D: Debited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Interest on capital borrowed during the construction period of a work is treated as part of the cost of the work and charged to Capital, since the asset is not yet earning revenue.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The classification of railway accounts broadly follows the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account.
2. The Government list applies to the Railways without any adaptation, the Railways having no commercial system of accounting.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: railway classification broadly follows the Government List of Major and Minor Heads. Statement 2 is false: the Railways adapt the list to their commercial system of accounting, with Major Heads like 3002 and 5002 and Plan Heads.

q: The cost of land acquired for the construction of a railway work is:

options.A: Charged to the working expenses of the year of acquisition
options.B: Treated as part of the capital cost of the work
options.C: Debited to the Development Fund in all cases
options.D: Shown permanently under a suspense head

e: The cost of land acquired for a railway work is treated as part of the capital cost of the work, since land is a capital asset acquired for the project.

q: A Vote on Account granted by the Lok Sabha is given legal effect through:

options.B: A resolution of the Railway Board
options.D: An Appropriation Act passed for the purpose

e: A Vote on Account granted by the Lok Sabha is given legal effect through an Appropriation Act passed for the purpose, authorising withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund for the part-year period.

q: Receipts from advertisements displayed at stations and on railway premises are classified under:

options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

e: Receipts from advertisements displayed at stations and on railway premises are not coaching or goods earnings; they are classified under Sundry Other Earnings.

q: Construction of a building for a training institute of the Railways is classified under Plan Head:
e: Construction of a building for a railway training institute falls under Plan Head 65, which covers Training and Human Resource Development works, including training infrastructure.

q: The annual Balance Sheet of a zonal railway is prepared from:

options.B: The balances appearing in the General Books (Ledger) of the railway
options.D: The Traffic Book

e: The annual Balance Sheet of a zonal railway is prepared from the balances appearing in the General Books (the Ledger), which collect all classified assets and liabilities of the railway.
